doc.title: Emile Barnes, George Guesnon, Little Brother Montgomery, Harold Dejan Interview, 1961-03-11

title: Little Brother Montgomery's visit from Chicago and trip to England
summary: Montgomery says he came to see Guesnon, George Lewis, Harold Dejan and his son in the Air Force, and describes about 31 days in England and Ireland.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, you know, Curly, what's happening, my friend, brother George Gano? Well, hello, little brother Montgomery, and how are you? Well, you know, Curly, what's happening, my friend, brother George Gano? There ain't nothing happening, you come all the way from Chicago to see me, that's right? Well, in a way I did, I came down to see you, George Lewis, and Harold Dijon, and among you boys around, and my son, mostly I came to see, out of the Air Force, Hamilton Air Base, little brother Montgomery, his name is here at Montgomery. Yeah, I know, I met him, he's a fine boy, and I mean, you just come out of England, didn't you? Yeah, I was in England for about 31 days, I was in London, and Belfast, I was in Ireland, Belfast, and around over there, I was in Nottingham, around in England, different than...
Yeah, Nottingham, that's where they whipping all that black-ass niggas ass about them old figs out there.
Now, Nottingham's where Robin Hood came from, take from the rich and give it to the poor.
